merger_name: INPEX – further interest in Bonaparte CCS JV
merger_description:
INPEX Bonaparte CCS Pty Ltd (**INPEX Bonaparte**), an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of INPEX Corporation (**INPEX**), proposes to acquire a 21% participating interest in the Bonaparte carbon capture and storage (**CCS**) joint venture (**Bonaparte CCS JV**) from Woodside Energy Ltd (**Woodside**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Bonaparte CCS JV is a contractual joint venture engaged in assessing the potential of establishing a CO2 storage facility within the G-7-AP block located off the northwest coast of the Northern Territory. Currently, the Bonaparte CCS JV is in the pre-final investment decision (**pre-FID**) phase.

The current parties to the joint venture are:

* INPEX Browse E&P Pty Ltd, another indirect wholly owned subsidiary of INPEX, with a participating interest of 53%, which is the operator of the Bonaparte CCS JV;
* TotalEnergies CCS Australia Pty Ltd (**TotalEnergies**) (26% participating interest); and
* Woodside (21% participating interest), whose interest is the target of the  Acquisition.

As a result of the Proposed Transaction, INPEX’s indirect participating interest in the Bonaparte CCS JV will increase to 74%.

INPEX is an oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. It engages in research, exploration, development, production and sale of oil, natural gas, other mineral resources and in related businesses. INPEX is also engaged in lower-carbon solutions, including CCS, as well as hydrogen and integrated power supply.

In addition to its interest in the Bonaparte CCS JV, INPEX has a minority interest in the Bayu-Undan CCS project, which is also pre-FID.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. INPEX (through its wholly owned subsidiaries) already owns
a majority interest in the Bonaparte CCS JV
b. the Acquisition does not create any current horizontal
overlap or vertical relationship in Australia, as the Bonaparte
CCS JV is not currently operational
c. there are a number of alternative projects in Australia
exploring carbon capture and storage opportunities,
including projects that are in active development or
construction.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
